tagline: Over Massanutten, across the South Fork, up into the Blue Ridge.
intro: The Page Valley is the valley of the South Fork of the Shenandoah, between Massanutten Mountain and the Blue Ridge. US 211 comes over Massanutten at New Market Gap, crosses the South Fork at Whitehouse Landing, skirts Luray, and climbs into Shenandoah National Park to Thornton Gap.

US 340 runs the length of the county, from the Rockingham line past Luray and through Big Spring to Overall, and back roads keep company with the river, Egypt Bend Road and River Road among them. Another, Bixlers Ferry and Fort Valley roads, heads out of Luray toward Camp Roosevelt.

moments.title: New Market Gap
moments.text: US 211 takes a curving climb, two lanes up and one down, to this 1,804-foot wind gap at the middle of Massanutten Mountain.

moments.title: Luray Caverns
moments.text: Five local men dug their way inside in August 1878 after noticing cool air rising from a sinkhole, and a lithophone called the Great Stalacpipe Organ now plays its stalactites.

moments.title: Thornton Gap
moments.text: A toll road crossed the Blue Ridge here from 1806, and a town called Beahm stood at the gap until the national park and the Skyline Drive arrived.
